other_failure_modes.name: Data Leakage in Cross-Validation Folds
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes feature transformations (specifically target encoding, imputation, and scaling) on the entire training set before performing K-Fold cross-validation. This leaks the target and feature distributions of the validation folds into the training folds, making the out-of-fold (OOF) predictions overly optimistic and ruining the meta-learner.

other_failure_modes.name: Discarding Test IDs for Submission
other_failure_modes.description: The agent drops the identifier column from the test set during processing but fails to save it. It then constructs the final submission file using a generic range index instead of preserving the original test IDs, which will likely cause the submission to fail evaluation.

other_failure_modes.name: Inefficient Hyperparameters Causing Timeout
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses an extremely small batch size (32) for a large number of epochs (400) inside a 5-fold cross-validation loop without adapting to dataset size, leading to excessive training time and causing the observed execution timeout.

summary: The solution properly establishes a hold-out validation set and uses K-Fold ensembling, but suffers from critical data leakage within the cross-validation loop because target encoding and scaling are applied to the entire training set prior to the CV splits. Additionally, it discards original test IDs, replacing them with a simple integer sequence, which will break the required submission format.
